step1_cross_config_generalization.note: Complete: model trained on config A evaluated on A (in-sample test split), B and C (cross-config, different mule topology/timing per PROJECT_SPEC.md).

step2_rule_only_baseline.note: Included inline in each config's 'rule_only' block above. Rule mirrors the generator's own terminal_choice heuristic per config: A=nearest_to_last_hop (proximity-based score), B=hotspot_avoidant (inverse recent-activity score), C=random_in_city (uniform score, no informative signal by construction -- see simulator/configs/{A,B,C}.yaml and model/baselines.py:rule_only_baseline for the exact per-config logic).

step3_label_noise_robustness.note: Simulator bakes differing label-noise rates into each config rather than exposing a standalone re-runnable noise knob (see simulator/configs/*.yaml label_noise blocks): A: false_negative_rate=0.05, false_positive_rate=0.02, label_delay_days in [0,14]. B: false_negative_rate=0.08, false_positive_rate=0.02, label_delay_days in [0,21]. C: false_negative_rate=0.10, false_positive_rate=0.04, label_delay_days in [0,10]. We report the model's metric degradation from A (lowest noise) to B and C (higher noise) as the robustness datapoint -- see step1_cross_config_generalization.results_by_config for the precision@10 values to compare directly. This conflates topology/timing shift with noise-rate shift (both change per config simultaneously), which is a real limitation of this thin slice: we cannot isolate 'noise effect alone' without a dedicated same-topology/different-noise config, which was out of scope for the prototype.

step4_real_data_separation.note: Out of scope for the Model agent -- owned by the Benchmark agent (model/benchmarks/, results/). This file and every metrics_config_*.json produced by the Model agent are exclusively simulated-data results and are never blended with any real-data benchmark numbers.

step5_realism_gap_statement: All metrics in this file are computed EXCLUSIVELY on simulator-generated data (simulator/configs/A.yaml, B.yaml, C.yaml) -- a seeded, rules-based generator calibrated against public NCRP/RBI/OSM summary statistics, not real bank transaction data. The simulator's mule-detection 'signal' (e.g. terminal proximity to recent activity, complaint density) is generated by the SAME family of heuristics the model is trying to learn (see simulator/configs/*.yaml terminal_choice rules), which inflates apparent model performance relative to a real deployment: a real adversary does not follow a known, stationary terminal_choice distribution, and real background traffic is not drawn from the same lognormal/poisson generators the model's features are tuned against. Cross-config generalization (A -> B, A -> C) is the best available proxy we have for this gap on a thin-slice prototype, but it is NOT a substitute for real-data validation (see the Benchmark agent's separate, real-data-only results for AMLworld/Elliptic/Chicago Crimes sanity checks, reported separately and never blended with these numbers). Precision@10 and lift figures here should be read as 'does the model learn the intended mule-activity signal at all', not as an estimate of real-world fraud-detection performance.
